systems.name: Home Assistant
systems.maker: Open source, backed by Nabu Casa
systems.radios: None built in. Add USB adapters for Zigbee, Thread, and Z-Wave
systems.best_for: Tinkerers and mixed-brand homes that want everything local
pros: Runs entirely in your home with no cloud required
Works with Z-Wave, Zigbee, Thread, Matter, and Bluetooth once you add the radios
The largest integration library of any platform here
Can share devices out to Apple Home, Google, and Alexa
cons: Steepest learning curve on this list
You handle updates and backups
Green has no radios built in, so adapters cost extra
Easy remote access and voice use a Nabu Casa subscription, or your own setup

systems.name: Apple Home
systems.hub: HomePod mini, HomePod, or Apple TV 4K
systems.best_for: iPhone households that want a polished, private setup
pros: The most polished app and Siri control
Strong privacy, with HomeKit traffic end-to-end encrypted
Home hubs double as Thread border routers and Matter controllers
Automations run on the home hub, not in a cloud
cons: Needs an iPhone or iPad; nothing for Android users
No Zigbee or Z-Wave without a third-party bridge
Automations are simpler than Home Assistant or Hubitat
Apple doesn't sell new HomePods or Apple TVs on Amazon

systems.name: Google Home
systems.hub: Nest Hub (2nd gen) or Google TV Streamer
systems.store_note: Amazon listings are resellers at inflated prices
systems.best_for: Android households and Google Assistant users
pros: Works on Android and iPhone
Nest Hub (2nd gen) and Google TV Streamer are Thread border routers and Matter hubs
Script editor for more advanced automations
Good voice control and camera support
cons: No Zigbee or Z-Wave
Many integrations still run through the cloud
Google has shut down smart home products and programs before
We couldn't find a fairly priced new hub on Amazon

systems.name: Amazon Alexa
systems.radios: Zigbee, Thread, Matter, Sidewalk, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth
systems.best_for: The cheapest, easiest start, especially with voice
pros: Echo Hub has Zigbee, Thread, and Matter built in
Works with more devices than any other voice assistant
Wall-mount dashboard with cameras, routines, and security controls
Sold and shipped by Amazon
cons: Most processing happens in Amazon's cloud
No Z-Wave
Routines are less flexible than Home Assistant, Hubitat, or Homey
Some features in the listing need Alexa+ or Ring subscriptions

systems.name: SmartThings
systems.radios: Zigbee, Matter, Wi-Fi (Z-Wave on V3 units, per the listing)
systems.local: Partly (Edge drivers run on the hub)
systems.best_for: Samsung households and people who want a middle ground
pros: Works on Android and iPhone
Zigbee and Matter built into the hub, plus Z-Wave on some versions
Many automations now run locally on the hub
Samsung TVs and appliances can join the same system
cons: Z-Wave support depends on which hub version you get
The platform has changed a lot; the 2022 move off Groovy broke custom device handlers
The app gets cluttered as you add devices

systems.name: Hubitat Elevation
systems.best_for: Z-Wave and Zigbee homes that want local control without building a server
pros: Everything runs on the hub, even with the internet down
Z-Wave 800 Long Range and Zigbee 3.0 built in
Rule Machine handles complex automations
Full functionality with no subscription, per the listing
cons: Interface feels dated next to Apple and Google
Matter over Thread devices need a separate border router
3.8-star rating on Amazon

systems.name: Homey Pro
systems.radios: Z-Wave Plus, Zigbee, Thread, Matter, Bluetooth LE, Infrared, Wi-Fi
systems.best_for: People who want every radio in one box and visual automations
pros: The most radios in one hub, including infrared
Homey Flow makes automations visual and approachable
Local-first processing
Works with Siri, Alexa, and Google
cons: The most expensive hub here
3.6-star rating on Amazon
Quality of brand apps varies
The cheaper Pro mini needs a Homey Bridge for Z-Wave, Bluetooth, and infrared
